Let \(p=2027\) and \(m=\frac{p-1}{2}=1013\). We work modulo \(p\).

Define

\[
F(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} \binom{2k}{k}2^k x^k \pmod p.
\]

We first identify this polynomial.

For \(k>m\), since \(p\le 2k<2p\), the numerator \((2k)!\) contains a factor \(p\), while the denominator \((k!)^2\) does not. Hence

\[
\binom{2k}{k}\equiv 0 \pmod p.
\]

For \(0\le k\le m\), we use the congruence

\[
\binom{2k}{k}\equiv (-4)^k\binom{m}{k}\pmod p.
\]

Indeed,

\[
\begin{aligned}
(-4)^k\binom{m}{k}
&=\prod_{j=1}^k \frac{-4(m-k+j)}{j} \\
&\equiv \prod_{j=1}^k \frac{2(2k+1-2j)}{j} \qquad (2m=p-1)\\
&=\frac{2^k(2k-1)(2k-3)\cdots 1}{k!}\\
&=\frac{(2k)!}{(k!)^2}=\binom{2k}{k}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Therefore

\[
\binom{2k}{k}2^k \equiv (-8)^k\binom{m}{k}\pmod p
\]

for \(0\le k\le p-1\), where \(\binom{m}{k}=0\) when \(k>m\). Thus

\[
F(x)\equiv \sum_{k=0}^m \binom{m}{k}(-8x)^k=(1-8x)^m \pmod p.
\]

Now

\[
S=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} k\binom{2k}{k}2^k \equiv F'(1)\pmod p.
\]

Since

\[
F'(x)=-8m(1-8x)^{m-1},
\]

we get

\[
S\equiv -8m(1-8)^{m-1}\pmod p.
\]

Here \(-8m=-4(p-1)\equiv 4\pmod p\), and \(m-1=1012\), so

\[
S\equiv 4(-7)^{1012}\equiv 4\cdot 7^{1012}\pmod{2027}.
\]

By Euler’s criterion,

\[
7^{1013}\equiv \left(\frac{7}{2027}\right)\pmod{2027}.
\]

Using quadratic reciprocity,

\[
\left(\frac{7}{2027}\right)
=-\left(\frac{2027}{7}\right)
=-\left(\frac{4}{7}\right)
=-1.
\]

Thus

\[
7^{1013}\equiv -1 \pmod{2027},
\]

so

\[
7^{1012}\equiv -7^{-1}\pmod{2027}.
\]

Since

\[
7\cdot 289=2023\equiv -4\pmod{2027},
\]

we have

\[
-4\cdot 7^{-1}\equiv 289\pmod{2027}.
\]

Therefore

\[
S\equiv 4\cdot 7^{1012}\equiv 289\pmod{2027}.
\]

\[
\boxed{289}
\]
